It ended alive about 6.8 m away, so the score was halved. **Estimated score: 10.5 × 0.5 / 12 ≈ 0.44.**\n\n**What was sampled (all 7 targets):**\n- On time: t3, t1, t5, d2 (discovered at tick 6), t4 and t2, worth 10.\n- Late: d1 (discovered at tick 11, deadline 21). I sampled it at tick 23 for 0.5. It could not be reached on time because the commands already queued ran through tick 18.\n\n**What went wrong:** I planned the whole mission against the time limit and never checked the battery total. Two things made it worse: d1's drive and sample were queued at tick 15 and could not be cancelled, and each sample costs 3.5 with the per-tick drain included.\n\nWhen the tick-22 telemetry arrived, the rover was 6.82 m from base. Reaching the 0.75 m radius needed at least 6.07 m of actual movement. After paying the drain for every remaining tick, only about 6.10 wheel metres of energy were left. That would only have worked with wheel slip under 0.5%, but measured slip had been 1–5%. Running the battery to zero scores 0, so I kept the rover where it was. It finished with about 6.1 battery left at tick 50.\n\nSkipping d1 and going straight home would have scored about 10/12 ≈ 0.83, roughly twice what I got. The fix is to budget battery for the whole route, including the return trip, before queuing extra targets.","time":{"start":1794628034884,"end":1794628034888}}}
